name: Drop Zone Safety-of-Flight Radio Net (UHF/VHF voice)
description: The voice radio channel between the Drop Zone Support Team and the drop aircraft. Deliberately limited-traffic by doctrine, not general coordination chatter: used for safety-of-flight matters (ATC directions, range clearance, unsafe surface conditions, mission changes) and to pass surface wind/limited weather observations. Mandatory for IMC/AWADS (instrument) drops; for standard visual drops, radio contact is used as needed rather than continuously. Represents a class of man-portable UHF/VHF AM radio (e.g. PRC-113-class equipment) generically — no specific real radio's exact frequency or crypto detail is modeled, consistent with the classification boundary (AGENTS.md Section 3).

commsLink.medium: UHF/VHF AM voice radio (representative class, e.g. PRC-113-class man-portable equipment), line-of-sight air-to-ground

doctrineSource.note: Army field manual, publicly mirrored on globalsecurity.org. Confirmed via web search on 2026-09-07 that: radio contact with the drop aircraft is limited to safety-of-flight requirements or issues affecting airborne force employment; the DZST passes surface wind/limited weather observations to inbound aircraft when radio contact is made; radio contact is mandatory for IMC/AWADS operations. Direct fetch of the page itself returned a 403 to this session's automated request — content is corroborated via search-result synthesis rather than an independent full read, and should be re-verified against the primary source before treating any additional specific claim from it as fact. commsLink is this dataset's structuring of the same 'UHF/VHF voice radio' fact already in this record's name/description, not a new claim.

name: Digital Situational Awareness System (ATAK-class, representative)
description: Represents a modern geospatial/situational-awareness capability in the style of ATAK (Android Team Awareness Kit) — a real, unclassified-discussable, DoD-adopted Android application (originally developed by the Air Force Research Laboratory) used for sharing positions, markers, and zone data via its Cursor on Target (CoT) protocol. Typically bearer-agnostic — cellular, satellite, or tactical mesh radio (e.g. Persistent Systems Wave Relay, Silvus-class MANET radios) rather than consumer Wi-Fi. Included as a plausible modern complement to the doctrinal voice radio net above. IMPORTANT: no source found this session documents ATAK specifically being used for CDS/airdrop drop-zone coordination in official Air Force materiel — this System is representative/illustrative only, not a doctrinally confirmed capability for this mission type.

commsLink.protocol: Cursor on Target (CoT), typically transported over UDP or TCP
commsLink.format: CoT XML event schema (point/position, marker, and zone data)

name: Rapid Dragon-class Palletized Effects Deployment System
description: A real, unclassified, publicly documented AFRL/USAF capability (program of record name: 'Dragon Cart'): a disposable, roll-on/roll-off deployment box that lets unmodified cargo aircraft (C-17, C-130, EC-130) airdrop palletized effects using standard aerial-delivery/CDS-style extraction, with no aircraft modification required. Originally demonstrated with palletized cruise missiles (JASSM-ER surrogates, 2021 C-17/EC-130 system-level tests), AFRL has since publicly stated the program is expanding from 'Palletized Munitions' to 'Palletized Effects' — explicitly including ISR platforms and humanitarian aid delivery. This mission's use of it to deploy ISR UAVs in a humanitarian-relief context is directly aligned with that stated public program direction, not a fictional stretch of an unrelated system.

doctrineSource.publication: Air Force Research Laboratory, "Rapid Dragon" / "Palletized Effects"
doctrineSource.note: Directly fetched from afresearchlab.com on 2026-09-07 (not a .mil domain, reachable this session). Direct quote: 'Palletized Effects has the potential to assist in multiple scenarios on the spectrum of conflict ranging from humanitarian relief to kinetic effects,' and Rapid Dragon 'is also expanding its Palletized Effects with Foreign Partners & Allies, which includes kinetic and non-kinetic effects; intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) platforms; contested logistics / cargo resupply.' Corroborated by Lockheed Martin's press release and Air & Space Forces Magazine coverage of the 2021 C-17 system-level demonstration and the 'Dragon Cart' program-of-record name.
